bucket.kairoute.gx1: {"voy:marrakech morocco":{"v":{"title":"Marrakech","listings":[{"type":"listing","name":"Marrakech Tourist Information","content":"","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.635556,"lng":-8.014167,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Medina","content":"The Medina is the old city quarter located within the sandstone city walls that give Marrakech the nickname the Red City. As an ancient hub, it contains a maze of narrow streets and outdoor marketplaces.","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.63318,"lng":-7.98869,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Djemaa El-Fna","content":"The highlight of any Marrakech night. Musicians, dancers, and story tellers pack this square at the heart of the medina, filling it with a cacophony of drum beats and excited shouts. Scores of stalls sell a wide array of Moroccan fare (see the Eat section) and you will almost certainly be accosted by women wanting to give you a henna tattoo. Amateur boxing matches are sometimes held. Enjoy the various shows, but be prepared to give some dirham to watch or take photos. By day it is largely filled with snake charmers and people with monkeys, as well as some of the more common stalls.","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.62604,"lng":-7.98903,"wikipedia":"Jemaa el-Fnaa","wikidata":"Q258348"},{"type":"see","name":"The Souks","content":"Markets of Marrakech, just adjacent to Place Djemaa El-Fna, are where you can buy almost anything, from spices to shoes, jellabas to kaftans, and tea pots to tagines. Undoubtedly, being a foreigner means you will end up paying higher prices than a native would, but be sure to bargain nonetheless. If you happen to run out of dirham, you will also find plenty of people in the souks who will eagerly exchange your dollars or euros (though a fair rate here is less likely than at an official exchange). All that said, the sellers here are much less aggressive than, say, Egypt, so have fun!","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.6271,"lng":-7.98727,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Koutoubia Mosque","content":"Named after the booksellers market that used to be located here. It is said that the minaret of the Koutoubia mosque is to Marrakech as the Eiffel Tower is to Paris. The minaret is visible from Gueliz which is connected to the Medina by Avenue Mohammed V. At night, the mosque is beautifully lit. The Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min founded the first mosque here in 1147 and built the present one beside it in 1158; the excavated remains of the first mosque can be seen on the esplanade next to it. The minaret was completed under Caliph Yaqub al-Mansur (1184 to 1199), and has inspired other buildings such as the Giralda of Seville and the Hassan Tower of Rabat. Non-Muslims are not allowed inside.","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.6237,"lng":-7.9935,"wikipedia":"Koutoubia Mosque","wikidata":"Q1137533"},{"type":"see","name":"Tanneries","content":"Visiting the tanneries can be an interesting experience. Even if some people tell you the area is only for locals, it is possible to visit the Tanneries without paying a youngster. After finding a tannery, ask one of the workers if you can visit it and take pictures","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.63367,"lng":-7.97862,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Saadian Tombs","content":"Saadian Tombs. The tombs were built in the 16th century as the dynastic necropolis of the Saadian dynasty. The complex includes the Chamber of the Twelve Columns, the Chamber of the Mihrab, the Chamber of the Three Niches and the garden tombs. The site was rediscovered in 1917 and subsequently restored and opened to visitors. The site is relatively compact and most visitors can see the main areas in 20–30 minutes. The Chamber of the Twelve Columns cannot be entered: visitors look in from an opening at its edge, originally a window in the eastern wall, and often have to wait for a turn. The entrance passage is narrow, so arriving early can help avoid queues.","hours":"generally 09:00–17:00, although visitors should check current information before travelling","price":"Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, children aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan nationals and residents: adult 30 dirham, child 10 dirham","url":"https://www.saadian-tombs.com","lat":31.617187,"lng":-7.988672,"wikipedia":"Saadian Tombs","wikidata":"Q2152745"},{"type":"see","name":"Moroccan Culinary Arts Museum","content":"If you are interested in food and eating culture, you will enjoy this museum. Audiovisual information about the rich culinary culture of Marocco, its ingredients, techniques and traditions. You can also touch and smell many things. They also sport a very well equipped cooking school.","hours":"","price":"","url":"https://www.moroccancam.com/","lat":31.62158,"lng":-7.98425,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Majorelle Gardens","content":"It provides an excellent respite from the hustle and bustle of the city streets, if not crowded by tourists as it sometimes is. The park was designed by the artist Jacques Majorelle in the 1920s and 1930s. Since 1980 the garden has been owned by Yves Saint-Laurent and Pierre Bergé. It boasts a collection of plants from around the globe, including what seems like every cactus species on the planet. Get here early to avoid the crowds. Inside the gardens is also the Berber Museum, which shows a slightly bigger and more modern presentation than the Dar Si Saïd. Advance bookings must be made online, it is not possible to buy a ticket at the site.","hours":"Oct-Apr: 08:00-17:30, May-Sep: 08:00-18:00, Ramadan: 09:00-17:00","price":"170 dirham, 30 dirham extra for the Berber Museum","url":"http://www.jardinmajorelle.com/ang/","lat":31.6415,"lng":-8.0029,"wikipedia":"Majorelle Garden","wikidata":"Q1395431"},{"type":"see","name":"Yves Saint Laurent Museum","content":"Advance bookings must be made online, it is not possible to buy a ticket at the site.","hours":"Thu-Tue 10:00 - 18:00","price":"120 dirham, combination ticket with Majorelle Gardens and Berber Museum 180 dirham, queues are far shorter here than at the gardens to buy tickets though you have to buy either a YSL Museum ticket or combination ticket","url":"https://www.museeyslmarrakech.com/en/","lat":31.6425,"lng":-8.0032,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":"Q30727522"},{"type":"see","name":"Dar Si Saïd Museum","content":"Museum set in an old palace with beautiful gardens. While somewhat run-down, it is worth seeing and houses many different artifacts from Morocco through the ages, such as wood carvings, musical instruments, and weapons. It is dedicated to the Moroccan craft industry of wood, gathering a very beautiful collection of popular art: carpets, clothing, pottery and ceramics. All these objects are regional, coming from Marrakech and all the south, especially from Tensift, High Atlas, Soussthe, Anti Atlas, Bani, and Tafilal.","hours":"10:00–18:00","price":"Locals: adult 10 dirham, child below 12 3 dirham; tourists: adult 30 dirham","url":"","lat":31.6234055,"lng":-7.9838624,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Ben Youssef Madrasa","content":"One of the largest madrassas in North Africa. It is a school attached to the Ben Youssef Mosque and is home to beautiful art and architecture. The present building was completed in 1564–1565 under the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib, on the site of an earlier Marinid madrasa. It closed as a school in 1960 and reopened to visitors in 1982. Look for the 11th-century Andalusi marble basin in the prayer hall.","hours":"09:00–19:00 daily (during Ramadan 09:00–16:30), closed for religious holidays","price":"Foreigners 50 dirham; Moroccans (with ID) 20 dirham; children under 12 10 dirham","url":"https://www.medersabenyoussef.ma/en/","lat":31.63203,"lng":-7.98618,"wikipedia":"Ben Youssef Madrasa","wikidata":"Q1560540"},{"type":"see","name":"El Bahia Palace","content":"An ornate palace complex built in the late 19th century, with courtyards, gardens, richly decorated rooms and traditional Moroccan architectural details. The palace was begun in the 1860s by Si Moussa, grand vizier to Sultan Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, and greatly expanded in 1894–1900 by his son Ba Ahmed, Grand Vizier to Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz. The main complex covers almost 2 hectares and has about 150 rooms. The main entrance is on Rue Riad Zitoun el Jedid. The palace is relatively close to other attractions in the southern Medina and can be reached on foot from Jemaa el-Fnaa. Arriving shortly after opening can be useful for visitors who want to avoid the busiest periods.","hours":"09:00–17:00","price":"Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham","url":"https://visitbahiapalace.com","lat":31.62089,"lng":-7.98414,"wikipedia":"Bahia Palace","wikidata":"Q2465115"},{"type":"see","name":"El Badi Palace","content":"The palace complex is extensive, with ruins, courtyards, underground passages and exhibitions. The terrace offers views over the surrounding Medina and the Atlas Mountains on clear days. Allow around 45–90 minutes to explore the main areas. Visitors should check current information before travelling. (updated Aug 2026)","hours":"09:00-17:00","price":"Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham","url":"https://badi-palace.com","lat":31.6187,"lng":-7.9853,"wikipedia":"Landmarks of Marrakesh#Badi_Palace","wikidata":"Q1277747"},{"type":"see","name":"The Menara gardens","content":"A mixture of orchards and olive groves surrounding the water reservoir with the central pavilion which is a popular sight on tourist postcards. Not a decorative garden, and now quite run down. The pavilion was built during the 16th-century Saadi dynasty, and renovated in 1869. It has a small cafe, but it is not open all hours. There are no toilets open when the cafe is closed.","hours":"09:00-17:00","price":"Free admission","url":"http://www.jardin-menara.com/","lat":31.61302,"lng":-8.02146,"wikipedia":"Menara gardens","wikidata":"Q1920259"},{"type":"see","name":"Jewish Cemetery","content":"The largest Jewish cemetery in Morocco, characterized by white-washed tombs and sandy graves. The men selling tickets are full of interesting information about the cemetery but you have to ask.","hours":"09:00-17:00","price":"10 dirham","url":"","lat":31.62006,"lng":-7.98018,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Slat Al Azama Synagogue","content":"Synagogue which is not only a place of worship with a beautiful open courtyard, but also includes interesting displays about Judaism's varied history in Morocco, including photos of Jews in the Berber Mountains.","hours":"09:00-19:00 (closed Sat)","price":"10 dirham","url":"","lat":31.620167,"lng":-7.982385,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":"Q3508008"},{"type":"see","name":"Marrakech Museum","content":"It's housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace, constructed at the end of the 19th century.","hours":"09:00-18:30","price":"50 dirham","url":"http://www.museedemarrakech.ma/","lat":31.63158,"lng":-7.98633,"wikipedia":"Marrakech Museum","wikidata":"Q3090631"},{"type":"see","name":"Musée de la Palmeraie","content":"In old agricultural buildings in the Palmeraie, made out of rammed earth. The architecture itself is interesting if you haven't seen it. It offers a small collection of contemporary art, with a room dedicated to Moroccan artists (also famous ones), the international ones are rather not top-notch. The gardens are nicely made and are good place to relax in quiet.","hours":"09:00-18:00?","price":"40 dirham","url":"","lat":31.650543,"lng":-7.947038,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Musee Farid Belkahia","content":"A museum dedicated to the renowned contemporary artist Farid Belkahia, showcasing different periods of his work","hours":"Mon-Sat","price":"","url":"","lat":31.6561111,"lng":-7.94805555,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Maison de la Photographie","content":"A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. Ticket is also valid for Museum of Mouassin Music.","hours":"","price":"80 dirham","url":"http://www.maisondelaphotographie.ma/","lat":31.63206,"lng":-7.98442,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"see","name":"Ali Ben Youssef Mosque","content":"The first mosque in Marrakesh was erected at this place by the Almoravid emir Yusuf ibn Tashfin in the 1070s. However, it was almost completely rebuilt in early 19th century by the Alaouite sultan Suleiman, with hardly any trace left of its original Almoravid or Almohad design. Non-Muslims are not allowed to enter it.","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":31.631925,"lng":-7.987161,"wikipedia":"Ben Youssef Mosque","wikidata":"Q4886745"},{"type":"see","name":"Agdal Gardens","content":"It consists of groves of orange, lemon, fig, apricot and pomegranate trees in rectangular plots, linked by olive-lined walkways. Together with the medina of Marrakech and the Menara Gardens, the Agdal Gardens were listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1985.","hours":"","price":"70 dirham for foreign adults","url":"","lat":31.606111,"lng":-7.979722,"wikipedia":"Agdal Gardens","wikidata":"Q392057"},{"type":"see","name":"Almoravid Koubba","content":"A very small but intricate domed pavilion, known for being the only surviving example of Almoravid religious architecture (early 12th century) in Marrakech. Located across the street from the Ben Youssef Mosque, it is believed to have been an annex of the former Almoravid mosque. It was excavated in the 20th century after being half-buried for centuries. The pavilion's exterior can be easily seen from the street, so paying for entry just lets you see its interior.","hours":"","price":"50 dirham","url":"","lat":31.6315,"lng":-7.9872,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"listing","name":"Jbilets Geological Site","content":"Explore the Berber village on a desert tour.","hours":"","price":"","url":"","lat":null,"lng":null,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"listing","name":"Anima garden","content":"One of the prettiest gardens in the world. Created by André Heller, it is true oasis when you’re weary of the medina hubbub. Book the official shuttle bus to get there and back for free.","hours":"","price":"","url":"https://www.anima-garden.com/","lat":31.40074,"lng":-7.82607,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"do","name":"Chez Ali Fantasia","content":"Horse show, acrobats on Arabian horses firing rifles in the air, horseback acrobatics, belly dancing, etc. It takes place at night in a huge imitation of an old castle.","hours":"","price":"€15","url":"https://www.fantasia-marrakech.com/","lat":31.70305,"lng":-8.02099,"wikipedia":"","wikidata":""},{"type":"do","name":"Stade de Marrakesh","content":"This is multi-use but mostly for football, with a capacity of 41,356.
